courses.title: The Corinthians Conversation
courses.description: Explore Paul’s relationship with the Corinthian church, examining conflict, community, and the call to embody Jesus, and considering how these conversations speak to challenges facing the church today.

courses.title: UMC 101
courses.description: Discover Methodism as a way of life, exploring its origins with John and Charles Wesley, its core beliefs and practices, and how the movement continues in a changing world.

courses.title: Five Misconceptions of Paul
courses.description: This four-week course revisits common misconceptions about the Apostle Paul, exploring his letters and context to better understand his faith, method, and enduring witness.

courses.title: Let's Talk About Christian Nationalism
courses.description: As America approaches 250, this course examines patriotism, nationalism, and Christian faith in a polarizing time, offering new ways to think about democracy, nationhood, and a peace-centered response.

courses.title: Paul's Vision of the Church
courses.description: This course explores the historical context, structure, and spiritual life of Paul’s churches—examining his metaphors for community, his call to edification and holiness, and his vision for the church’s mission in the world.

courses.title: Lies My Pastor Told Me
courses.description: In this course, Brent Strawn—author of Lies My Preacher Told Me—challenges common misconceptions about the Old Testament. If you’ve ever questioned its relevance, wrestled with its laws or violence, or struggled with its portrayal of God, this class offers fresh insight into why the Old Testament still matters today.

courses.title: Resurrection Stories
courses.description: This course will investigate and compare the resurrection stories from all four gospels. We will explore how the gospel writers use the resurrection appearances of Jesus in creating portraits of Jesus for a variety of audiences in the early Christian community. To conclude the course, we will reflect on how these four unique portraits of the Risen Jesus work together and speak to the Christian community of today.

courses.title: Black Theology and Faith
courses.description: What does faith look like when shaped by struggle, hope, and justice? In this four-week course, Dr. Noel Erskine introduces key themes of Black theology (e.g., liberation, reconciliation, and baptism) and explores how faith flourishes across cultures. Open to all, this course invites honest reflection on how theology is lived, shared, and continually reimagined.

courses.title: The Corinthians Conversation
courses.description: In this course, we explore the issues that the church in Corinth faced and the Apostle Paul’s conversations with them. We also look at the particulars of the situations and how Paul consistently emphasizes the “big picture”—the Corinthians’ embodiment of Jesus. This class will also look beyond the issues to the emotional relationship between Paul and the church in crisis. Finally, we ask how the conversation between Paul and Corinth can offer support and guidance to the church in our context as the church navigates the particular conflicts of the 21st century.

courses.title: How the Bible Actually Works
courses.description: This course explores how the Bible works, introducing interpretive tools from the Christian tradition to help you read Scripture with confidence while engaging difficult texts across the canon.

courses.title: Encountering Scripture: Psalms
courses.description: This four-session course explores the Psalms as ancient Israel’s prayerbook—honest, poetic, and deeply spiritual. We’ll examine their language, theology, and relevance for shaping a rich, vulnerable, and grounded spiritual life today.

courses.title: The Courage to Follow: The Life and Witness of Dietrich Bonhoeffer
courses.description: This four-week course introduces Bonhoeffer’s life and The Cost of Discipleship, inviting us to consider integrity, courage, and an unashamed commitment to Christ as we practice honest, accountable, and justice-oriented faith.

courses.title: How the Bible Actually Works
courses.description: This five-week course explores how the Bible works—its history, genres, and truth claims—to help you read Scripture with greater confidence, nuance, and curiosity. No prior training needed—just a willingness to explore.

courses.title: Women of Advent
courses.description: Women of Advent highlights the often-overlooked stories of the women who prepared the way for Christ, revealing their courage, faith, and prophetic witness. This course invites participants to reflect on how their lives illuminate the hope, longing, and promise at the heart of the Advent season.

courses.title: The PreacHER and the Word
courses.description: This four-week course invites participants to engage the dynamic intersection of women’s history, theology, and preaching. Led by esteemed scholar and preacher Dr. Teresa Fry Brown, the course explores the rich legacy of women in ministry, from the struggle for the right to preach to the complexities of ordination and authority. Learners will explore the diverse theological foundations women draw from, reflect on how to cultivate an authentic preaching voice, and develop tools for sermon preparation, delivery, and analysis. Whether you're discerning your call or seeking to deepen your practice, this course offers space to honor the voices of women who proclaim the Word.

courses.title: Hebrew Insights: 12 Words that Will Transform Your Understanding of the Old Testament
courses.description: Unlock the Old Testament by exploring 12 key Hebrew words—like shalom, justice, and salvation. This course offers practical insights into biblical meaning, language, and culture—no Hebrew experience required, just curiosity and a desire to read Scripture with fresh eyes.

courses.title: Faith in the Wild
courses.description: Wilderness is more than just a desert—it’s a place of struggle, growth, and unexpected encounters with God. Together, we’ll explore how the Bible uses wilderness as a powerful symbol and find out what these stories of pain and provision can teach us today.

courses.title: Re-Gendering [Fox Center Key Word Lecture Series]
